top_sub_skill_patterns.note: Judgment call: canceling common factor in fraction → EE.5 or just EE.3?
Factor-then-cancel classified as factoring vs rational expression

disagreement_analysis.dominant_pattern: EE.5 boundary: 71 of 98 sub-skill disagreements involve Pass 2 tagging EE.5 where Pass 1 did not, or substituting it for EE.3/EE.4. This is a genuine taxonomy judgment about whether rational-expression simplification is a separate sub-skill from the factoring/exponent step that enables it.
disagreement_analysis.distractor_note: Low distractor agreement (36.4%) is expected: distractor cluster assignment requires inferring the specific error a student made from a wrong answer option, which is inherently more ambiguous than solution-path tagging.

mis_skilled_questions.note: All 351 questions are in the EE skill and received at least one EE sub-skill tag in both passes

pass1_session.note: Token-level tracking not available for fork agents

pass2_session.method: independent CCR sibling session with fork agents

methodology.pass1: Fork-agent manual mathematical derivation: each agent reads the question text/options, solves the problem step-by-step, identifies sub-skills and clusters from the solution path, and for MCQs reverse-engineers distractor error patterns.
methodology.pass2: Independent CCR sibling session with fork agents using identical methodology. Session had no access to Pass 1 results. Agents derived solutions independently.
methodology.comparison: Exact set-match on sub_skill_ids, cluster_ids, and distractor_clusters (option_key+cluster_id pairs) per question.
